about.accuracy_matched: p203's rule: the fastest prior point meeting the bound if its HOTA is not above Tetris's, else the most accurate Pareto-optimal prior point with HOTA not above Tetris's, which may miss the bound (per_dataset.*.prior.meets_bound).

bounds.leap_fit: HOTA >= LEAP's best HOTA on the dataset

about.checks: port_check: this script's values on p203's inputs against p203's own functions (must match, or the run stops). manuscript_check: the same values rounded to 0.1 against the submitted macros. leap_runtime_effect: p203 macros that change when LEAP's runtime is deduplicated.
about.dominance: Secondary rule from the feedback script: per prior system meeting the bound, the fastest Tetris configuration with HOTA at least that prior point's HOTA.
about.estimates: LEAP's CalDoT1 and CalDoT2 runtimes are the mean of two recorded runs per video (an estimate of one run). Every other number is measured.
about.ground_truth: B3D1-B3D4 HOTA is scored against automatic ground truth (tiled RetinaNet detections tracked by OC-SORT, Section 7.1). Rerun this script after R1.O1 replaces it with human-verified labels. CalDoT1, CalDoT2, and Amsterdam use OTIF's detection labels (tracks linked by OC-SORT) and are outside R1.O1.
about.leap_fit: Provisional with LEAP (see leap_status). LEAP's best HOTA is far below the other systems', so this bound admits nearly every Tetris and OTIF configuration; Tetris over OTIF there compares points of very different HOTA.
about.leap_status: Provisional. LEAP's HOTA comes from p140_otif_transform.transform_tracking_json, which sets frame = list index; LEAP's outputs are longer than the clips and hold many same-frame identical boxes (leap_checks.output_alignment), so the conversion is unverified (R1.O2, "document the HOTA conversion"). Do not quote any LEAP or leap_fit number, or "LEAP misses the 5%/10% bound", until the conversion is fixed and rescored. LEAP's runtime is deduplicated here (leap_checks.runtime).

manuscript_rules.compareAccuracyMatchedSpeedup{Min,Max}{F: accuracy_matched (abstract l.25, introduction l.106-110 and l.138, Section 7 l.208-211, conclusion l.25). Its matched prior point may miss the bound (accuracy_matched.<bound>.per_dataset.*.prior_meets_bound).
manuscript_rules.comparePriorFailDatasetsFivePct, compare: ranges.<bound>.prior_fail and prior_meets (abstract l.21, introduction l.104 and l.137, Section 7 l.202, conclusion l.24).
manuscript_rules.compareSpeedup{Min,Max}{FivePct,TenPct}: ranges.<bound>.tetris_vs["fastest prior"], the shared-bound rule; no live sentence quotes it.

about.measured: Each system's fastest test-split configuration whose HOTA meets a per-dataset bound, its speedup over the reference pipeline, Tetris's speedup over each prior system meeting the same bound, and p203's accuracy-matched speedup.
about.ratios: Speedups and ratios divide unrounded throughputs, then round to 0.1 (common.operating_points).
about.selection: Operating points are chosen by test-split HOTA among the test runs of each system's validated Pareto configurations (p135), the manuscript's method. Candidate pools differ by system (configurations): Tetris has tens of configurations per dataset, OTIF about ten, LEAP one.

throughput.leap: inference_total - decode per test video from LEAP's raw stat CSV, so decoding is excluded; repeated runs of a video are averaged (leap_checks.runtime). p140 uses the total row instead.
throughput.otif: runtime_total from OTIF's stat CSV (p140 normalize_otif_stat_csv). OTIF's per-stage columns (seg, detect, track, decode) sum to more than runtime_total, so stages overlap and its decoding time cannot be separated out.
throughput.prior_fps: Prior systems' throughput is the test split's frame count (our clips) over their runtime, as in evaluation/p200_compare_compute.py and p203, not the frames the system decoded.
throughput.tetris_and_reference: throughput_fps from p130's tradeoff table: test frames over the stage runtimes p121 sums, without the ops total_frame_time, read_frame, save_canvas, and save_mapping_files, and without read and retrieve in p020 classification.

about.ties: Bounds are inclusive (HOTA >= bound; p203/p204 test round(loss, 12) <= loss bound, which differs only within 1e-12 of the bound and is checked by port_check). Throughput ties go to the more accurate configuration, then the smaller config name. Maxima over datasets break ties by p204's dataset order (CONFIG EXEC.DATASETS), as pandas idxmax does.
